title: Distinguish never-sent retained recovery attempts from abandoned sends in checkpoint lineage
outcome: Distinguish never-sent retained recovery attempts from abandoned sends in checkpoint lineage
acceptance: Checkpoint recovery preserves exact original and attempt provenance while distinguishing a retained attempt positively known not to have reached the send boundary from a possibly-sent or unknown attempt.

Deterministic tests exercise failed persistence before PossiblySent, a later allocated attempt and a restart; never-sent attempts do not fabricate historical uncertainty or authorize replay of genuinely uncertain work.
The representation and reader-floor classification are independently reviewed; no attempt history is silently erased or relabelled as a producer certificate.
